_meta.purpose: Research-backed overrides for known projects. These supplement deterministic rules; they do not overwrite raw source records.

pine-belt-landfill-cell7.displayName: Pine Belt Landfill — Cell No. 7 Construction

requiredChecks.detail: Prospective prime bidders must register as plan holders to obtain official documents/addenda.
Verify Mississippi contractor classifications appropriate to excavation and landfill/liner scope.

pine-belt-landfill-cell7.whyItMatters: The published work explicitly contains major dirt-work scope, but the liner/leachate package makes prime pursuit more specialized than ordinary excavation.
pine-belt-landfill-cell7.nextAction: Immediately review the bid documents and planholder list. If prime readiness is not already in place, target planholders/prime bidders for excavation, hauling, grading, or liner-support pricing.
pine-belt-landfill-cell7.firstAction: Open the designated planroom immediately and review addenda, planholder list and the excavation/liner/leachate bid items.
pine-belt-landfill-cell7.secondAction: If landfill-prime qualifications are not already in place, call planholders and offer excavation, hauling, grading and liner-support pricing.
pine-belt-landfill-cell7.stopIf: The remaining bid runway is too short to price responsibly, or the available package cannot be separated from specialty liner/leachate obligations.

approximately 14,112 tons of asphalt items in the base bid

requiredChecks.detail: Prime bids are accepted only in the name of a bidder on the official planholder list.
The notice requires a certified check or bid bond equal to 5% of the total bid.
The work is governed by the Mississippi Standard Specifications for State Aid Road and Bridge Construction.

msproc-46147.whyItMatters: This is a real heavy-highway job with excavation, stone and roadbed-reclamation quantities, but the published quantities are dominated by asphalt and striping. For the demo sitework contractor, it is more credible as a subcontract/partner lead than as a default prime pursuit.
msproc-46147.nextAction: Get the official plans/proposal and target planholders or paving primes with pricing for excavation, crushed stone, roadbed reclamation, granular material and hauling rather than treating the full job as a natural sitework prime.
msproc-46147.firstAction: Download/order the official plans and proposal and isolate excavation, crushed stone, roadbed reclamation, granular material and hauling quantities.
msproc-46147.secondAction: Use the official planholder list to approach paving primes with a discrete sitework/base package.
msproc-46147.stopIf: The dirt/base package is too small relative to mobilization distance or planholders are already carrying the work internally.

requiredChecks.detail: Prospective prime bidders must register with the designated plan website as a plan holder.
Official addenda and notifications are issued through the designated plan website.

laurel-citywide-paving.whyItMatters: The $3.5M published project includes explicit water/sewer work, creating a credible utility/sitework subcontract opportunity even when the contractor is not an asphalt prime.
laurel-citywide-paving.nextAction: Open the official planroom, register as a planholder if considering prime pursuit, and identify the utility/sitework bid items and active planholders to quote.
laurel-citywide-paving.firstAction: Register/login at the designated planroom and inspect the bid schedule for water-service, sewer-service, pavement-removal, base-repair and restoration items.
laurel-citywide-paving.secondAction: Use the planholder list to identify paving primes and send a focused utility/sitework quote invitation before the bid date.
laurel-citywide-paving.stopIf: The bid schedule contains no meaningful utility/sitework package or the contractor cannot meet the requested subcontract schedule.

requiredChecks.detail: Project value exceeds Mississippi's commercial-license threshold; verify appropriate contractor classification.
Review project manual/drawings for actual earthwork, drainage, base, and paving quantities before treating inferred sitework as confirmed.

pineview-parking.whyItMatters: This is a smaller public works package within the target geography and may be closer to the scale at which a local sitework contractor can realistically participate.
pineview-parking.nextAction: Obtain the project manual/drawings from Neel-Schaffer and quantify grading, drainage, aggregate base, hauling, and paving responsibilities before making the prime/sub decision.
pineview-parking.firstAction: Obtain the project manual and civil drawings and quantify clearing, grading, drainage, aggregate base, curb/paving and hauling.
pineview-parking.secondAction: If prime readiness is verified, decide bid/no-bid. Otherwise identify planholders/GCs and quote the site package.
pineview-parking.stopIf: Civil quantities are too small to justify mobilization or the prime requirements exceed the contractor's verified license/bonding capacity.

fitEvidence: a general contractor is publicly soliciting bids on its planroom

requiredChecks.detail: Civil/site sheets must be reviewed; current public notice does not prove the excavation/sitework package.

aaa-resource-center.recommendedContact: Kim Reed — Flagstar Construction, Brandon Office
aaa-resource-center.whyItMatters: A contractor planroom shows Flagstar actively soliciting this project, which creates a concrete subcontract outreach path even though the exact civil package still needs to be verified.
aaa-resource-center.nextAction: Contact Flagstar's listed bid contact, ask whether they are carrying the civil/sitework package, and obtain the relevant civil drawings/specs before pricing.
aaa-resource-center.firstAction: Call the listed GC/planroom contact and ask whether the civil/sitework package is open to subcontract pricing.
aaa-resource-center.secondAction: Only download and estimate the civil sheets after the GC confirms the package is available.
aaa-resource-center.stopIf: The GC is self-performing sitework or already has the package committed.

greene-road-maintenance.whyItMatters: Legitimate heavy-civil work, but geography and likely paving-heavy quantities make it a lower-priority fit for the current demo contractor profile.
greene-road-maintenance.nextAction: Review quantities only if the contractor is willing to travel beyond the preferred radius or can quote a discrete earthwork/hauling package.

clarkco-trail.whyItMatters: The work appears to include legitimate clearing, grading and drainage, but Quitman is just outside the demo contractor's 75-mile preferred radius.
clarkco-trail.nextAction: Treat as an optional regional pursuit: obtain the official plans, verify quantities, and only spend estimating time if travel/logistics fit the contractor's current workload.
clarkco-trail.firstAction: Only pull the plans if the contractor is willing to work beyond the 75-mile preference; confirm clearing, grading and drainage quantities.
clarkco-trail.secondAction: Compare likely margin against travel/mobilization burden before spending estimating time.
clarkco-trail.stopIf: Travel/mobilization erodes margin or the civil quantities are not substantial.

walthall-orphan-wells.displayName: MSOGB Orphaned Well Plugging — Adams & Walthall Counties
fitEvidence: current MSOGB IFB covers nine wells in Adams and Walthall Counties
primary scope is plugging, remediation and reclamation of orphaned oil and gas wells

requiredChecks.detail: Do not treat this as ordinary excavation/sitework. Review the current MSOGB IFB for oil-and-gas well-plugging experience, technical procedures, site requirements and financial-security requirements.

walthall-orphan-wells.whyItMatters: The reclamation portion uses dirt-work skills, but the prime contract is fundamentally an oil-and-gas well-plugging package. A normal excavation contractor should not spend estimating time on it unless it already has the specialty capability or a qualified teaming partner.
walthall-orphan-wells.nextAction: Archive for the demo contractor unless it already performs regulated oil-and-gas well plugging or has a qualified teaming partner. If specialty capability exists, use the current MSOGB active-procurement page and IFB documents.
